papers.title: Processing enhances the anti-hepatocellular carcinoma effect of Momordicae Semen via remodeling chemical composition and regulating the Akt/mTOR/STAT3 pathway.
papers.abstract: Momordicae Semen (MS) is a traditional medicinal herb with reported antitumor potential. However, the impact of processing on its chemical composition and the underlying mechanisms against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to characterize processing-induced chemical changes and elucidate the bioactive constituents and molecular pathways responsible for improved anti-HCC effects. UPLC-QTOF/MS was used to compare chemical differences between crude and processed samples. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation
papers.summary: This study shows that processing Momordicae Semen (a traditional medicinal herb) enhances its anti-liver cancer effects by altering its chemical composition. The processed herb appears to work by regulating the Akt/mTOR/STAT3 signaling pathway, as revealed through chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and molecular simulations.

papers.title: Experimental and computational investigation to elucidate the structure and dynamics of amino acid-based deep eutectic system.
papers.abstract: Deep Eutectic Solvents derived from amino acids are considered environmentally friendly because they are biodegradable, recyclable, and exhibit acceptable levels of toxicity. These solvents have various applications in various fields, such as biocatalysis, electrochemistry, extraction, and pharmaceuticals. Glutamine is an amino acid commonly found in human blood, and glycerol is a conventional solvent with rapid biodegradability. In this study, biodegradable amino acids based deep eutectic solvent (DES) was prepared from the mixture of glutamine and glycerol at a 1:3 (Glu: Gly) molar ratio, an
papers.summary: This study investigates the structure and dynamics of a biodegradable deep eutectic solvent (DES) made from glutamine and glycerol, using experimental and computational methods. The findings provide insights into the molecular interactions and behavior of this environmentally friendly solvent, which has potential applications in biocatalysis, electrochemistry, and pharmaceuticals.

papers.title: Comparative Structure-Based Analysis of Predicted BZD9L1 Binding Modes Across Human Sirtuins.
papers.abstract: Sirtuins (SIRTs) are NAD+-dependent enzymes implicated in cancer and other diseases, but the high conservation of their catalytic sites complicates the development of isoform-selective inhibitors. BZD9L1 is a benzimidazole-based sirtuin inhibitor with previously reported activity against SIRT1 and SIRT2. However, its potential interactions with other human sirtuin isoforms remain incompletely characterized. Here, we applied a comparative structure-based modelling framework integrating homology modelling, molecular docking, and targeted experimental assessment to investigate plausible binding m
papers.summary: This study uses computational modeling and docking to predict how the sirtuin inhibitor BZD9L1 binds to different human sirtuin isoforms, revealing potential interactions beyond SIRT1/2. The work provides a structural rationale for isoform selectivity and may guide the design of more specific sirtuin inhibitors for cancer therapy.

papers.title: Identification of Natural Flavonoids Targeting PLK-1 as Potential Anti-Metastatic Agents: A Computational Approach.
papers.abstract: This study combines ligand- and structure-based in silico strategies to predict the inhibitory activity of natural flavonoids on the Polo-Like Kinase-1 (PLK-1) enzyme as candidate anticancer agents. This enzyme participates in mitosis and is overexpressed in cancer cells. Furthermore, it has been shown to have important implications for tumor metastasis, and its inhibitors are attractive starting points for drug development. First, classification models are developed using linear discriminant analysis and a multilayer perceptron neural network. Models with accuracy greater than 80%, validated
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to identify natural flavonoids that may inhibit PLK-1, an enzyme involved in cancer cell division and metastasis. The authors developed classification models with high accuracy to predict inhibitory activity, suggesting these compounds as potential anti-metastatic drug candidates.

papers.title: Sequence determinants of pathogenicity in glucose-6-phosphatase linked to glycogen storage disease type 1a.
papers.abstract: Glycogen storage disease type 1a (GSD1a) is an autosomal recessive Mendelian disorder that can be caused by missense variants in glucose-6-phosphatase catalytic subunit 1 (G6PC1). Although hundreds of missense variants have been identified, the vast majority are of unknown clinical significance, and the molecular mechanism(s) of bona fide pathogenic variants are ill-defined. We combine bioinformatic data and clinical associations with the protein language model AlphaMissense to guide mechanistic exploration of 78 missense variants at 55 residue positions using robust biochemical and biophysica
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying glycogen storage disease type 1a (GSD1a) by combining bioinformatic and clinical data with the AlphaMissense protein language model to guide experimental characterization of 78 missense variants in G6PC1. The work aims to define sequence determinants of pathogenicity and clarify the functional consequences of variants of unknown significance.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Foreign Body Responses to Neural Electrodes and Surface Biofunctionalization Strategies for Interface Modulation.
papers.abstract: Long-term implantable neural electrodes underpin brain-machine interfaces, deep brain stimulation, epilepsy monitoring, and closed-loop neuromodulation. Following chronic implantation, however, the foreign body response (FBR) at the electrode-tissue interface remains a major constraint on long-term performance, as reflected by increased interfacial impedance, lower signal-to-noise ratios, fewer resolvable units, and higher stimulation thresholds. This deterioration arises from interrelated events that include implantation injury, protein adsorption, blood-brain barrier disruption, complement a
papers.summary: This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying the foreign body response (FBR) to chronic neural electrode implants, which degrades their performance over time. It also discusses surface biofunctionalization strategies—such as coatings and chemical modifications—that aim to modulate the electrode-tissue interface and improve long-term biocompatibility and function.

papers.title: CdS-Based Photocatalysts for Antimicrobial Applications: From Quantum Dots to Z-Scheme Heterojunctions-Mechanisms, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: The chronic overuse of antibiotics has accelerated the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, creating a global public health crisis as conventional therapies fail against multidrug-resistant pathogens spreading through water and food chains. Cadmium sulfide (CdS) has been established as an important visible-light-driven photocatalyst for antibacterial applications. This brief review systematically examines the structure-property relationships governing CdS-based antibacterial materials, including crystallographic polymorphs (cubic sphalerite and hexagonal wurtzite), morphological diversi
papers.summary: This review examines cadmium sulfide (CdS)-based photocatalysts for antibacterial applications, covering their structural properties, mechanisms, and design strategies such as quantum dots and Z-scheme heterojunctions. It highlights their potential as an alternative to antibiotics against drug-resistant bacteria, while discussing challenges and future directions.

papers.title: FDA-Approved Drug Repurposing as p53 Mutants Rescue Candidates Using Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Simulations.
papers.abstract: The restoration of mutant p53 stability is a highly sought-after strategy in targeted cancer therapy. This study presents a structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics approach to nominate FDA-approved drugs as candidate stabilizers of mutant p53 for downstream experimental validation. A virtual screening library of FDA-approved compounds was docked against three representative p53 mutants (7DHY, 7DHZ, and 7V97) to evaluate their binding potential. The prioritized candidates demonstrated consistent, multi-conformer binding affinities. Protein-ligand interaction profiling revealed
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations to identify FDA-approved drugs that could stabilize mutant p53, a key target in cancer therapy. The authors docked a library of approved compounds against three p53 mutants and prioritized candidates with consistent binding affinities and favorable interaction profiles, providing a shortlist for experimental validation.

papers.title: Solvent Interaction Analysis: A New Lens for Protein Structure and Diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Aqueous two-phase systems (ATPSs) provide a versatile, fully aqueous platform for probing solute-water interactions and protein structure. This review first surveys the diversity and phase behavior of biphasic aqueous systems formed by polymers and salts. We describe how phase diagrams characterize ATPS formation and composition and how both polymer chemistry and salt identity, rather than molecular size alone, govern phase separation by modulating the solvent properties of water. Building on a modified binodal model, we show that phase separation and solute partitioning can be understood in t
papers.summary: This review introduces aqueous two-phase systems (ATPSs) as a versatile platform for studying protein structure and solute-water interactions, emphasizing that polymer chemistry and salt identity, rather than molecular size alone, govern phase separation. It presents a modified binodal model to explain phase behavior and solute partitioning, offering a new perspective for protein diagnostics and structural analysis.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics and Electron Density Topology Reveal Ligand-Specific Interaction Patterns at the Dopamine D2 Receptor.
papers.abstract: The dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) is one of the principal therapeutic targets for the treatment of schizophrenia and other neuropsychiatric disorders. Understanding how ligands with different pharmacological profiles interact with D2R is essential for the rational design of safer and more effective antipsychotic drugs. In this work, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations combined with Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) analysis were employed to investigate the electronic nature of protein-ligand interactions in D2R embedded in a neuronal membrane environment. Representative agonists (dopam
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations and quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) analysis to characterize how different ligands interact with the dopamine D2 receptor in a neuronal membrane environment. The findings reveal ligand-specific electronic interaction patterns that could inform the rational design of safer and more effective antipsychotic drugs.

papers.title: Linear Residual Network Modeling for Anti-HIV-1 Activity Prediction and Docking-Validated Design of Biphenyl-DAPY-Based NNRTIs.
papers.abstract: To predict the anti-HIV-1 activity of biphenyl-DAPY-based non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) analysis was conducted. Using the heuristic method (HM) for descriptor selection, four predictive models were established: support vector regression (SVR), kernel ridge regression, linear mixed-kernel SVR, and Linear Residual Network (LRNet). Rigorous validations, including leave-one-out cross-validation, fivefold cross-validation, and Y-randomization tests, confirmed their reliability. The LRNet model exhibited the best perfo
papers.summary: This study develops quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models to predict the anti-HIV-1 activity of biphenyl-DAPY-based NNRTIs, with a novel Linear Residual Network (LRNet) model showing the best performance. The models were rigorously validated and used for docking-validated design of new compounds, providing a computational tool for accelerating NNRTI drug discovery.

papers.title: AlphaFold 3 prediction of TCR mimic Fv - pMHC complex structures and their validation and optimization.
papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibody-derived chimeric antigen receptors (CAR) that mimic T‑cell receptors (TCR) on binding to peptide-major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) and activating T‑cell functions hold great promise for the development of effective immunotherapy. This study applied AlphaFold 3 (AF3) to model the quaternary structures of TCR mimic antibody variable fragment (TCRm Fv) complexed with NY-ESO-1157-165/HLA-A*02:01. Benchmark study suggested that reliable TCRm Fv-pMHC structures were achieved by AF3 with high confidence. Toward NY-ESO-1/A2-specific CAR clones, AF3 prediction revealed their i
papers.summary: This study evaluates AlphaFold 3's ability to predict the quaternary structures of TCR-mimic antibody variable fragments bound to peptide-MHC complexes, using NY-ESO-1/HLA-A*02:01 as a benchmark. The predictions achieved high confidence and were validated experimentally, and the approach was used to optimize CAR clones targeting this complex. This work demonstrates the utility of AlphaFold 3 for structure-based design of TCR-mimic immunotherapies.

papers.title: Trans-interface coupling in the tetrameric enzyme underlies allosteric control in Escherichia coli biosynthetic threonine deaminase.
papers.abstract: Allosteric regulation in biosynthetic L-threonine deaminase (BTD) has long been attributed to effector-induced conformational changes. Here, we identify a trans-interface coupling mechanism that regulates the active site architecture of EcIlvA, the BTD homolog of Escherichia coli. Starting from a low-activity, regulatory-domain-truncated variant (EcIlvA1-335, termed CDL) that retains only the catalytic domain and the native linker region, we combined computational screening with experimental selection and directed evolution to identify a variant (designated HSG) bearing three mutations in the
papers.summary: This study reveals a new allosteric control mechanism in E. coli biosynthetic threonine deaminase, where coupling across the tetramer interface regulates active site architecture. Using computational screening and directed evolution, the authors identified a variant with three mutations that alter this trans-interface coupling, providing insights into how effector-induced conformational changes are transmitted in this enzyme.

papers.title: In-silico study of active phytochemicals and molecular mechanism of Hydrocotyle javanica Thunb.in treating MDR enterobacterial infection.
papers.abstract: Enterobacterial infections being severe, with a high mortality rate, particularly affecting ICU patients, and 80% newborns. These infections have multifactorial multi-drug resistance (MDR) mechanisms, which frequently causes current antibiotic therapies to fail, mortality rate remains high, and creating an urgent need for alternative multi-targeted therapies, such as plant-derived compounds to restore clinical effectiveness. This study aims to discover novel anti enteric compounds in Hydrocotyle javanica Thunb. (H. javanica) belongs to Apiaceae family and understanding their interaction mechan
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to identify active phytochemicals from Hydrocotyle javanica Thunb. and predict their molecular mechanisms against multidrug-resistant enterobacterial infections. The findings suggest that plant-derived compounds may serve as multi-targeted alternatives to conventional antibiotics, potentially restoring clinical effectiveness against resistant strains.

papers.title: Toward Material-Specific Peptides From in Silico Guided Peptide Engineering to Target PET in the Presence of PS.
papers.abstract: Synthetic polymers are indispensable but pose major recycling challenges, particularly in mixed plastic waste streams. Enzymatic recycling offers a promising route to specific polymer depolymerization into oligomers and monomers. This requires controlling molecular recognition at polymer interfaces. Material-binding peptides (MBPs) can enhance catalytic degradation by directing catalysts to specific polymer surfaces, yet strategies for engineering polymer specificity remain limited. Here, we introduce a computational-experimental workflow for designing polymer-selective MBPs. Molecular dynamic
papers.summary: This study presents a computational-experimental workflow for designing material-binding peptides (MBPs) that selectively target polyethylene terephthalate (PET) even in the presence of polystyrene (PS). By combining molecular dynamics simulations with experimental validation, the authors demonstrate a strategy to engineer polymer-specific peptides, which could enhance enzymatic recycling of mixed plastic waste.

papers.title: Quinazolinone-triazole hybrids as multi-target-directed ligands for Alzheimer's disease: discovery of potent and selective MAO-B inhibitors with cholinesterase modulating activity.
papers.abstract: A new series of quinazolinone-triazole hybrids (QTHs, 5a-n) was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as potential multi-target-directed ligands for Alzheimer's disease. All synthesized compounds were screened against human monoamine oxidase A (MAO-A) and monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B). The obtained results revealed pronounced selectivity toward MAO-B, with IC50 values ranging from 0.65 to 7.51 µM, while exhibiting negligible MAO-A inhibition (IC50 > 40 µM). Compounds 5a, 5d, 5g, 5h, and 5m emerged as the most potent and selective MAO-B inhibitors and were subsequently evaluated for inhibition of
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of quinazolinone-triazole hybrids as multi-target-directed ligands for Alzheimer's disease. Several compounds showed potent and selective inhibition of monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) with IC50 values in the low micromolar range, and also exhibited cholinesterase modulating activity, suggesting potential as leads for Alzheimer's therapy.

papers.title: Vitamin B1-catalyzed green synthesis and antiplasmodial evaluation of 2-amino-7-hydroxy-4-aryl-4H-chromene-3-carbonitrile derivatives: computational insights into putative PfNDH2 targeting.
papers.abstract: A green and sustainable synthetic protocol was developed for the preparation of a previously unreported series of 2-amino-7-hydroxy-4-aryl-4H-chromene-3-carbonitrile derivatives (PPA1-PPA5) using vitamin B1 (thiamine hydrochloride) as an inexpensive and environmentally benign organocatalyst under mild aqueous ethanol conditions. The synthesized derivatives were comprehensively characterized by FTIR, 1H/13C NMR, HRMS, and elemental analyses, and subsequently evaluated for their in vitro antiplasmodial activity against the chloroquine-sensitive Plasmodium falciparum 3D7 strain together with thei
papers.summary: This study reports a green, vitamin B1-catalyzed synthesis of novel chromene derivatives and evaluates their antiplasmodial activity against Plasmodium falciparum, with computational insights into their potential targeting of PfNDH2. The compounds show promise as antimalarial leads, combining sustainable chemistry with biological evaluation.

papers.title: The crystal structure of the activin B:Fst288 complex and computational insights into the broad antagonistic activity and specificity of follistatin.
papers.abstract: Members of the transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) family regulate essential biological processes, and their activity is tightly controlled by extracellular antagonists like follistatin 288 (Fst288). While Fst288 potently inhibits several ligands, including activins A and B, GDF8, and GDF11, the structural basis for its interaction with activin B (ActB) has remained largely uncharacterized. This lack of data has limited our understanding of how Fst288 achieves such broad inhibitory activity while maintaining ligand-specific selectivity. In this study, we resolved the crystal structure of the
papers.summary: This study resolves the crystal structure of the activin B:Fst288 complex, revealing how follistatin achieves broad inhibition of TGF-β ligands while maintaining specificity. Computational analyses provide insights into the molecular determinants of Fst288's antagonistic activity, advancing our understanding of extracellular regulation of this signaling family.

papers.title: Viral Nuclease Inhibitors: Small molecule disruptors of the UL12 alkaline nuclease display broad anti-herpes virus activity.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) UL12 encodes a highly conserved 5' → 3' alkaline exonuclease that is essential for the production of infectious virus. Together with the viral single-stranded DNA-binding/annealing protein ICP8, UL12 functions as a two-component recombinase that mediates recombination-dependent viral DNA replication. Here, we present the crystal structure of the catalytic domain of the HSV alkaline nuclease (UL12), which provides the first view of an α-herpesvirus alkaline nuclease. Using this structure, we optimized a series of small-molecule viral nuclease inhibitors (VNIs) tha
papers.summary: This study presents the first crystal structure of the HSV-1 UL12 alkaline nuclease catalytic domain and uses it to optimize small-molecule inhibitors that disrupt UL12 function. These viral nuclease inhibitors show broad anti-herpesvirus activity, suggesting a new potential therapeutic strategy against herpesviruses.

papers.title: Sabinene attenuates inflammation and oxidative stress in CFA-induced arthritis: In vivo and in silico evidence implicating TLR4/NLRP3/NF-κB signaling.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic immune-mediated disease in which persistent inflammation and oxidative stress contribute to progressive joint damage. This study evaluated the prophylactic effects of sabinene in complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA)-induced arthritis and explored potential molecular associations using integrated in vivo and computational approaches. Rats were allocated to vehicle control, arthritic control, piroxicam, or sabinene groups (15, 30, or 60 mg/kg; n = 6/group); sabinene was administered orally beginning 30 minutes before CFA injection and continued for 28 days. Paw
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that sabinene, a plant-derived monoterpene, reduces inflammation and oxidative stress in a rat model of rheumatoid arthritis, with in silico evidence suggesting it acts by modulating TLR4/NLRP3/NF-κB signaling. The findings support sabinene as a potential therapeutic candidate for RA, though further studies are needed to confirm clinical utility.

papers.title: An integrated approach: green extraction technique optimization, mechanistic study, and bioactivity profiling of four flavonoids from Epimedium sagittatum.
papers.abstract: In this study, a novel strategy for simultaneous extraction of four key flavonoids (epimedin A, epimedin B, epimedin C, and icariin) from Epimedium sagittatum using deep eutectic solvent-ultrasound assisted extraction (DES-UAE) was developed. Initially, 24 kinds of DESs were produced, a proline-lactic acid system demonstrated optimal extraction efficiency. The ideal parameters were established by single-factor experiments and response surface methodology optimization: water content of 29%, molar ratio of 1 : 1.9, liquid-solid ratio of 32 : 1 mL g-1, ultrasound power of 280 W and extraction tim
papers.summary: This study develops an optimized green extraction method using deep eutectic solvents combined with ultrasound to efficiently extract four bioactive flavonoids from Epimedium sagittatum, identifying proline-lactic acid as the best solvent system. The work includes mechanistic insights and bioactivity profiling, offering a sustainable alternative for natural product extraction.

papers.title: Structure-based TCR-pMHC binding prediction and generalization to unseen peptides.
papers.abstract: The interaction between T-cell receptors (TCRs) with the peptide-bound major histocompatibility complex (MHC) intricately impacts the functional specificity of T-cell-mediated adaptive immune response. Consequently, implication in immunotherapy has contributed to the ever-growing computational methods for TCR recognition, which have recently attracted structure-based approaches due to advancements in protein structure modeling. Despite access to structural information of the predicted binding interface, graph neural network (GNN)-based TCR-pMHC binding specificity classifiers tend to show poor
papers.summary: This paper presents a structure-based approach for predicting TCR-pMHC binding specificity, leveraging predicted structural information of the binding interface. The authors address the challenge of generalizing to unseen peptides, which is critical for immunotherapy applications. The work highlights the limitations of current GNN-based classifiers and proposes improvements for better generalization.

papers.title: Expression, purification, crystallization and structure solution of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase from the babesiosis infective agent Babesia bovis.
papers.abstract: Babesia bovis is a species of apicomplexan hemoparasitic protozoa that can be transmitted by ticks, causing a global cattle disease. As it depends mainly on the glycolytic pathway for energy production and life cycle maintenance, glycolytic enzymes are possible targets for drug development against Babesia. Glyceraldehyde-3-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (GAPDH) has been one of such targets, against several parasitic organisms. It performs the reversible oxidative phosphorylation of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate to 1,3-bisphospho-D-glycerate in the presence of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide. The proto
papers.summary: This paper describes the expression, purification, crystallization, and structure solution of glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) from Babesia bovis, a tick-borne parasite causing cattle disease. The structural characterization of this glycolytic enzyme provides a foundation for structure-based drug development against babesiosis.

papers.title: Discovery of Novel Druggable Binding Pockets on SARS-CoV-2 PLpro via Fragment Screening and Insights for Structure-Based Inhibitor Design.
papers.abstract: Coronaviruses are a large family of viruses capable of causing severe respiratory diseases, with recent outbreaks posing major threats to global public health. The SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) is an essential viral enzyme involved in viral replication and host immune evasion, making it an attractive target for antiviral drug development. However, no PLpro-targeted drugs have yet been approved. Here, we employed a fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) strategy combined with crystallographic screening and identified 23 fragment compounds with well-defined electron density. These fragme
papers.summary: This study used fragment-based drug discovery and crystallographic screening to identify 23 fragment compounds binding to SARS-CoV-2 PLpro, revealing novel druggable binding pockets. The findings provide structural insights that could guide the design of new antiviral inhibitors targeting this essential viral enzyme.

papers.title: Improving Activity and Stability of Candida boidinii Formate Dehydrogenase Through Rational Active Site Engineering.
papers.abstract: Formate dehydrogenases represent a highly attractive tool for nicotinamide cofactor regeneration to drive biocatalytic reductions and oxygenations by NADH-dependent oxidoreductases with formate as a cheap, atom-economic terminal reductant. However, despite the clear benefits over other recycling systems, native FDHs remain rather unpopular, mainly due to their intrinsic, low specific activity. While the active site architecture is generally highly conserved across many FDHs from very diverse origins, smaller patterns of dissonance in the active site's vicinity can serve as hotspots for the rat
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This paper describes rational engineering of the active site of Candida boidinii formate dehydrogenase to improve its activity and stability, addressing a key limitation (low specific activity) that hinders its use in cofactor regeneration for biocatalysis. The authors identify specific residues near the active site that act as hotspots for mutation, leading to enhanced enzyme performance.

papers.title: Hierarchical Discrete Representations for Coarse-to-Fine Protein Conformation Generation.
papers.abstract: Protein conformation generation remains a fundamental challenge in structural biology and machine learning. Proteins are highly dynamic macromolecules, and their functions are governed not only by static 3D structures but also by their conformational flexibility. Therefore, generating a diverse ensemble of physically plausible structures is crucial for modeling conformational heterogeneity, characterizing intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), and supporting structure-based drug discovery. However, existing generative models often operate in continuous coordinate space. This approach makes
papers.summary: This paper introduces a hierarchical discrete representation approach for generating protein conformations, enabling coarse-to-fine modeling of structural ensembles. The method addresses limitations of continuous coordinate-space generative models, potentially improving the generation of diverse, physically plausible conformations relevant to intrinsically disordered proteins and drug discovery.

papers.title: Computational alanine scanning with GBSA and interaction entropy: a review of methodologies and applications in protein-protein and protein-ligand binding.
papers.abstract: Computational alanine scanning (CAS) has emerged as a powerful in silico strategy for identifying binding hot spots in protein-protein and protein-ligand complexes, addressing the limitations of experimental alanine scanning mutagenesis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of CAS methodologies, with particular focus on the integration of GBSA (molecular mechanics/generalized born surface area) and the Interaction Entropy (IE) method. Traditional CAS approaches have been hampered by the systematic neglect of entropic contributions or computationally prohibitive entropy calculations vi
papers.summary: This review covers computational alanine scanning (CAS) methods, focusing on the integration of GBSA and interaction entropy to predict binding hot spots in protein complexes. It addresses how these approaches overcome the limitations of experimental mutagenesis and traditional entropy calculations, providing a practical guide for researchers.

papers.title: Integrated computational and preclinical evaluation of drug repurposing candidates for KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: KRAS mutations, particularly KRAS G12C, pose significant therapeutic challenges in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) due to limited inhibitor efficacy and rapid resistance. Drug repurposing offers a time and cost-effective strategy to identify alternative therapeutic options targeting KRAS-driven signalling. A structure-based drug repurposing approach was employed to screen FDA-approved compounds targeting key regulators to the MAPK signalling pathway and computationally modelled for potential engagement with the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket. Computational analyses including virtual screening,
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based drug repurposing approach to screen FDA-approved compounds for potential activity against KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer, focusing on the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket. The authors identify candidate drugs through virtual screening and computational modeling, then validate their effects in preclinical models, offering potential alternative therapeutic options for KRAS-driven cancers.

papers.title: Nitrogen Fixation by MoSn3 and MoSn5 Clusters.
papers.abstract: The Haber-Bosch process (HBP) for the conversion of nitrogen into ammonia is arguably one of the most important chemical reactions in human history because it is the basis for the large-scale production of fertilizers and hence of global food production. Nevertheless, the HBP contributes in a decisive manner to the production of CO2 and other global warming gases, since it is an extremely energy-intensive process. Consequently, the development of alternative conditions to reduce its negative environmental impact is of the highest priority. In this study, we investigate the detailed mechanism o
papers.summary: This study computationally investigates the mechanism of nitrogen fixation by MoSn3 and MoSn5 clusters, proposing them as potential alternatives to the energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. The findings may inform the design of new catalysts for ammonia production with lower environmental impact.

papers.title: New Structures of Human Formylglycine-generating Enzyme Reveal Features Important for Catalysis, Disease and Structure-based Drug Design.
papers.abstract: The formylglycine-generating enzyme (FGE) post-translationally modifies the active site of all human sulfatases. Mutations in the SUMF1 gene encoding FGE may lead to catalytically inactive FGE or destabilize the protein. The resulting lack of sulfatase modification causes the rare disease multiple sulfatase deficiency (MSD). Previously, FGE required elastase treatment for crystallization and the structures lacked copper, although FGE is a copper-dependent enzyme. Here, we show that highly active human FGE purified from insect cells natively contains one copper ion and we report six new crystal
papers.summary: This study presents new crystal structures of human formylglycine-generating enzyme (FGE), revealing that the enzyme natively contains a copper ion and highlighting structural features important for catalysis, disease mutations, and drug design. These findings advance understanding of FGE function and provide a basis for developing therapies for multiple sulfatase deficiency.

papers.title: DeepPNI: a language- and graph-based model for mutation-driven protein-nucleic acid binding energetics.
papers.abstract: Protein-nucleic acid interactions (PNIs) are central to fundamental biological processes, and mutations can disrupt these interactions by altering local structural features and binding free energy. Here, we present DeepPNI, a deep learning regression model that integrates sequence- and structure-based features to estimate mutation-induced changes in binding free energy in protein-nucleic acid complexes. The model was developed using a comprehensive dataset of 1754 mutations spanning protein-DNA and protein-RNA complexes, representing one of the largest curated datasets for PNI binding free ene
papers.summary: DeepPNI is a new deep learning model that predicts how mutations change the binding strength of protein-nucleic acid interactions (like protein-DNA and protein-RNA). It combines sequence and structural information and was trained on a large curated dataset of 1,754 mutations, making it a valuable tool for understanding mutation effects in these critical biological processes.

papers.title: Sparsomycin inhibits translation through a conserved mechanism across all domains of life.
papers.abstract: Sparsomycin (SPA) is a broad-spectrum inhibitor of protein synthesis with activity across all three domains of life. Although SPA has long been known to target the ribosomal peptidyl transferase center (PTC), previous structural studies suggested that SPA binds differently to bacterial ribosomes compared to their archaeal and eukaryotic counterparts-an unexpected conclusion given the high evolutionary conservation of the ribosomal catalytic center. Here, we show that SPA inhibits a majority of elongation-competent bacterial ribosomal complexes and present X-ray crystal structures of Thermus th
papers.summary: This study reveals that the antibiotic sparsomycin inhibits protein synthesis through a conserved mechanism across all domains of life, contrary to previous suggestions of domain-specific binding. Using X-ray crystallography and biochemical assays, the authors demonstrate that sparsomycin binds uniformly to the ribosomal peptidyl transferase center in bacterial, archaeal, and eukaryotic ribosomes, resolving a long-standing discrepancy and reinforcing the evolutionary conservation of this drug target.

papers.title: Broad-Spectrum Multi-Epitope Design Targeting Conserved Hantavirus Glycoproteins (Gn/Gc): Chimeric Antigen Engineering and Structural Mapping.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses, the etiological agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), represent a high-risk zoonotic threat with substantial global health impact. Currently, there is no FDA-approved vaccine. The viral surface glycoprotein (GP) is crucial for host cell entry and is regarded as a key target for vaccine development. However, its variability among hantavirus species limits the effectiveness of conventional vaccine strategies. Epitope-based vaccines offer a promising alternative by enabling the design of broadly protective constructs. In this
papers.summary: This study presents a computational design of a broad-spectrum multi-epitope vaccine targeting conserved regions of hantavirus glycoproteins (Gn/Gc), using chimeric antigen engineering and structural mapping to address viral variability. The approach offers a promising strategy for developing a vaccine effective against multiple hantavirus species, potentially filling the gap left by the lack of an FDA-approved vaccine.

papers.title: Physicochemical, Rheological, and Sensory Characterization of Gluten-Reduced Cookies Enriched with Amaranth and Chickpea Flours.
papers.abstract: The global transition toward plant-based diets necessitates the development of sustainable, nutritionally enriched, and gluten-reduced bakery products. This study evaluated the techno-functional, nutritional, and sensory impacts of substituting wheat flour at levels of 30%, 50%, and 70% with a binary blend of amaranth (Amaranthus caudatus) and chickpea (Cicer arietinum) flours in short-dough cookies. Dough's thermo-mechanical behavior was characterized using the Mixolab Chopin+ protocol and correlated with Texture Profile Analysis (TPA) and consumer acceptability (n = 60) via Principal Compone
papers.summary: This study investigates the effects of substituting wheat flour with amaranth and chickpea flours at 30%, 50%, and 70% levels in gluten-reduced cookies, assessing dough rheology, texture, and consumer acceptability. The findings provide insights into optimizing plant-based, gluten-reduced bakery formulations while maintaining sensory quality.

papers.title: Humanized Anti-PD-1 Antibodies Generated Using The Conditional Kernel-Elastic Autoencoder.
papers.abstract: The human immune system excels at generating highly effective antibodies through natural selection and somatic hypermutation, but adapting these antibodies for therapeutic use, referred to as "antibody medicine-likeness", requires careful consideration of biochemical and physiological properties. Traditional redesign methods are often slow and limited in scope. In this study, we introduce a machine learning-based approach to evolve new anti-PD-1 antibodies within a chemically informed latent space using a conditional kernel-elastic autoencoder (CKEA) between nivolumab and pembrolizumab, both o
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a machine learning approach using a conditional kernel-elastic autoencoder (CKEA) to generate humanized anti-PD-1 antibodies by evolving sequences in a chemically informed latent space between nivolumab and pembrolizumab. The method aims to improve 'antibody medicine-likeness' more efficiently than traditional redesign approaches.

papers.title: Seed-Guided De Novo Design Expands the Structural Diversity of Antitoxin Protein Binders.
papers.abstract: De novo design of protein binders targeting extended, multi-site interaction surfaces remains difficult for current generative methods, which often produce limited structural diversity and predominantly helical topologies. Here, we advance diffusion-based binder design by guiding protein backbone generation through ″seeds,″ which are PDB-derived fragments selected for geometric complementarity to the target surface. To test this approach, we computationally generated seed-guided binders of the bacterial toxin RelE. RelB, the native antitoxin of RelE, engages two distinct interfaces with high s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a seed-guided diffusion-based method for de novo protein binder design that uses PDB-derived fragments to guide backbone generation, enabling targeting of extended, multi-site interaction surfaces. The approach was tested on the bacterial toxin RelE, successfully generating binders with greater structural diversity than existing methods, including non-helical topologies, and achieving high affinity and specificity.

papers.title: Interpreting Protein Language Models: high attention sites predict functional regions.
papers.abstract: Computational proteomics has revolutionized biomedical research, guiding targeted experimental exploration to accelerate protein-based mechanistic discovery. Protein Language Models (PLMs) enable scalable, resource-efficient study; through large-scale training on only primary protein sequences, PLMs generate vector representations of protein structure that have been shown to capture biochemical, evolutionary, and structural properties. A core component of PLMs is the attention mechanism, which specifically captures long-range interactions across a protein sequence in attention matrices. Using
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates whether attention patterns in protein language models (PLMs) can identify functionally important regions in proteins. The authors find that high-attention sites correlate with known functional regions, suggesting PLMs can be used to predict functional sites without requiring structural or evolutionary data.

papers.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Predictions of Mutation-Induced Fold Switching.
papers.abstract: Many proteins are known to adopt multiple distinct folded states which are often associated with key functional behavior. A predictive understanding of the properties of such fold-switching or metamorphic proteins can provide insights into protein dynamics and energetics, and enable the design of complex protein functions and molecular machines. Recently developed deep learning modeling tools, including AlphaFold, have led to dramatic increases in accuracy for prediction of protein structures from sequence, but their performance for prediction of point mutant effects or fold switching is uncle
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint benchmarks deep learning protein structure prediction tools, including AlphaFold, for their ability to predict the effects of point mutations on fold switching in metamorphic proteins. The authors find that current deep learning methods have limited accuracy for this challenging task, highlighting a gap between structure prediction and predicting conformational changes.

papers.title: Evaluation of Uliginosin B as a Modulator of the Ras Pathway: In Vivo Evidence From Caenorhabditis elegans and In Silico Insights.
papers.abstract: Previously, in vitro studies have suggested a possible antiproliferative action of uliginosin B (ULI B), a dimeric acylphloroglucinol isolated from Hypericum species. However, no in vivo evidence of this effect has been found yet. Therefore, the aim is to evaluate its possible interaction in the Ras pathway using the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans and computational models. For the in vivo assays, we used a strain with a gain-of-function in the let-60 gene, which is a human Ras homologous protein that leads to the formation of tumorous multivulva. The experimental tests indicated that a single
papers.summary: This study provides the first in vivo evidence that uliginosin B (ULI B), a compound from Hypericum plants, can modulate the Ras signaling pathway, using a C. elegans model with a tumorous multivulva phenotype caused by a Ras gain-of-function mutation. The compound reduced the phenotype, and computational modeling supported a potential interaction with Ras, suggesting a possible mechanism for its antiproliferative effects.

papers.title: Host immune network-guided reverse vaccinology approach for prioritizing candidate antigens in Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Schistosoma japonicum-associated liver fibrosis (SSLF) remains a major cause of long-term morbidity in schistosomiasis, even in post-control or low-transmission settings. While most vaccine development efforts have focused on reducing parasite burden, few approaches have incorporated host pathology related to liver fibrosis. This study developed an in silico strategy that combined host single-cell analysis with reverse vaccinology to guide the exploratory screening of parasite antigens with potential relevance to SSLF. Single-cell transcriptomics of fibrotic and control human liver tissues was
papers.summary: This study presents a computational strategy that combines host single-cell transcriptomics with reverse vaccinology to prioritize Schistosoma japonicum antigens potentially involved in liver fibrosis. By integrating host immune network data, the approach offers a new way to screen vaccine candidates that may also address fibrosis-related pathology, not just parasite burden.

papers.title: Effects of L-glutamic acid on wheat starch structure and functionality: multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: L-Glutamic acid (L-Glu) is central to carbon-nitrogen metabolism, yet its ability to improve starch quality by regulating grain metabolism and by directly modulating starch structure remains unclear. In this study, we integrated a field experiment with an in vitro experiment and combined untargeted metabolomics, microscopy, structural characterization, physicochemical and processing property analyses, and molecular dynamics simulations. It was found that under drought, L-Glu spraying reprogrammed the grain metabolome, with pathway enrichment in aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis and starch/sucrose me
papers.summary: This study shows that spraying L-glutamic acid on wheat under drought conditions improves starch quality by reprogramming grain metabolism and directly modifying starch structure, as revealed by integrated field and in vitro experiments with multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations. The findings suggest L-Glu could be used to enhance starch functionality in crops facing water stress.

papers.title: From in silico screening to experimental verification: Identification of novel umami peptides from tamarind (Tamarindus indica L.) seed proteins and their validation in enzymatic hydrolysates.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides are key contributors to food flavor enhancement. In this study, novel umami peptides from tamarind seed proteins were identified using an integrated strategy combining in silico screening and experimental validation. A virtual peptide library was screened based on physicochemical properties and bioactivity, yielding six candidates (VSDY, DGIDF, AKNVSDYL, YNDPHC, VPPD, and NDPHCQY). Molecular docking and dynamics simulations revealed stable binding to the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3 via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, with binding affinities of -7.9 to -8.8 kcal/mol.
papers.summary: This study identified six novel umami peptides from tamarind seed proteins using a combined in silico and experimental approach. The peptides showed stable binding to the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3 and were validated in enzymatic hydrolysates, offering potential new flavor enhancers.

papers.title: Exploration of Length and Hydrophobicity Requirements for Optimal α-Amylase Secretion in Bacillus subtilis Based on Rational Design.
papers.abstract: The secretory (Sec) pathway is the major pathway of Bacillus subtilis for protein export from the cytoplasm to the extracellular milieu. An amino-terminal signal peptide is required to initiate protein translocation across the cytoplasmic membrane via Sec. Generally, Sec pathway signal peptides of B. subtilis are around 20-30 amino acids long and tend to be relatively hydrophobic compared to signal peptides from other organisms. In view of the importance of signal peptides for high-level secretory protein production, understanding how signal peptide structure and length influence the efficienc
papers.summary: This study investigates how the length and hydrophobicity of signal peptides affect α-amylase secretion in Bacillus subtilis, using rational design to identify optimal parameters. The findings provide practical guidance for engineering signal peptides to enhance secretory protein production in this industrial host.

papers.title: Experimental, Genomic, and Structural Evidence Supporting Putative PET-Hydrolases in Thermophilic Bacteria Isolated From Hot Springs in Cajamarca, Peru.
papers.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste represents a major environmental challenge due to limited recycling solutions. Thermophilic bacteria from geothermal environments harbor diverse enzymatic machinery adapted to extreme conditions, offering promising biocatalysts for plastic degradation; however, biological resources from Peru and other South American countries remain scarce. We characterized four bacterial strains isolated from two geothermal sites in Cajamarca, Peru, screened for PET hydrolysis at 50°C. Whole-genome sequencing using hybrid assembly achieved near-complete circular genomes.
papers.summary: This study characterizes four thermophilic bacterial strains from hot springs in Peru, using whole-genome sequencing to identify putative PET-degrading enzymes. The findings expand the known diversity of thermophilic PET hydrolases and highlight geothermal environments as a source of novel biocatalysts for plastic recycling.

papers.title: A destination-driven framework for nanoparticle-enabled targeted protein degradation.
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) offers a revolutionary paradigm to eliminate disease-driving proteins. Given the distinct technical requirements and challenges associated with degrading intracellular versus extracellular proteins, we classify existing TPD strategies based on subcellular localization into two categories: intracellular TPD (iTPD), which targets proteins within the cytoplasm and nucleus, and extracellular TPD (eTPD), which focuses on membrane-bound and secreted proteins. This destination-based framework facilitates precise technology selection and rational design by aligning m
papers.summary: This review proposes a framework for classifying targeted protein degradation (TPD) strategies based on the subcellular destination of the target protein—intracellular (iTPD) versus extracellular (eTPD)—to guide the rational design of nanoparticle-enabled TPD approaches. It highlights the distinct technical requirements and challenges for degrading proteins in different cellular compartments, aiming to facilitate precise technology selection.

papers.title: Tuning protein corona on nucleic acid nanodrugs for targeted delivery.
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle-based delivery systems hold transformative potential for nucleic acid therapeutics. However, the fate of nucleic acid nanodrugs (NANDs) in vivo differs significantly from that observed in vitro, directly impacting their therapeutic efficacy. Upon introduction into biological fluids, NANDs rapidly adsorb proteins onto their surfaces, forming an assembled adsorption layer known as the protein corona (PC). This PC critically influences the physicochemical properties of NANDs and consequently governs their subsequent biological interactions. This review comprehensively introduces the
papers.summary: This review discusses how the protein corona, a layer of proteins that forms on nucleic acid nanodrugs in biological fluids, critically affects their in vivo behavior and therapeutic efficacy. It highlights strategies to tune the protein corona for improved targeted delivery, offering a comprehensive overview of this key barrier in nanomedicine.

papers.title: Edge-aware GAT-based protein binding sites prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein binding sites is crucial for understanding biomolecular interaction mechanisms and for the rational design of drug targets. Traditional predictive methods often struggle to balance prediction accuracy with computational efficiency when capturing complex spatial conformations. To address this challenge, we propose an Edge-aware Graph Attention Network (Edge-aware GAT) model for the fine-grained prediction of binding sites across various biomolecules, including proteins, DNA/RNA, ions, ligands, and lipids. Our method constructs atom-level graphs and integrates
papers.summary: This paper introduces an Edge-aware Graph Attention Network (GAT) for predicting protein binding sites across diverse biomolecules (proteins, DNA/RNA, ions, ligands, lipids). The model constructs atom-level graphs and integrates edge-aware attention to improve prediction accuracy and computational efficiency, addressing limitations of traditional methods.

papers.title: N-Alkylated Monoterpene Indole Alkaloid Derivatives as Chemotherapy Adjuvants That Overcome P-glycoprotein-Mediated Multidrug Resistance in Cancer Cells, Spheroids and Patient-Derived Colorectal Cancer Organoids.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy efficacy is often limited by multidrug resistance (MDR), largely driven by P-glycoprotein (P-gp). This study aimed to evaluate previously prepared N-alkylated dregamine and tabernaemontanine derivatives as potential adjuvants to overcome P-gp-mediated chemoresistance.
papers.summary: This study evaluates N-alkylated derivatives of the monoterpene indole alkaloids dregamine and tabernaemontanine as adjuvants to overcome P-glycoprotein-mediated multidrug resistance in cancer. The compounds were tested in cancer cells, spheroids, and patient-derived colorectal cancer organoids, showing potential to enhance chemotherapy efficacy by inhibiting P-gp.

papers.title: Integrating multi-omics and deep learning to explore the active ingredients and molecular mechanisms of Cinnamomum migao volatile oil in the treatment of coronary heart disease.
papers.abstract: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is a major cardiovascular disease. Cinnamomum migao volatile oil (CM-VO) is traditionally used for CHD, but its active basis and mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-omics and deep learning approach to identify the active ingredients and molecular mechanisms of Cinnamomum migao volatile oil (CM-VO) in treating coronary heart disease (CHD). The findings reveal potential bioactive compounds and key pathways, providing a scientific basis for the traditional use of CM-VO in CHD therapy.

papers.title: Molecular dynamics simulation study on macroscopic mechanical deterioration and microscopic hydration mechanism of mudstone.
papers.abstract: Aiming at the common problem of borehole instability caused by mineral hydration in water-sensitive mudstone formations during petroleum drilling, this paper conducts a multi-scale study by integrating X-ray diffraction, triaxial mechanical experiments, and molecular dynamics simulation methods. It systematically analyzes the mineral composition of mudstone, the evolution law of its mechanical properties after hydration, and the microscopic mechanism of hydration. The results indicate that: ① The montmorillonite content in the mudstone dominates its strong water sensitivity, leading to a sharp
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-scale approach combining X-ray diffraction, triaxial mechanical experiments, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how water hydration degrades the mechanical properties of mudstone, a common cause of borehole instability in petroleum drilling. The findings show that montmorillonite content is the key driver of water sensitivity, and the simulations reveal the microscopic hydration mechanisms responsible for macroscopic mechanical deterioration.

papers.title: Exploring the causal role and mechanism of galanin in glioblastoma: integration of mendelian randomization, network analysis, molecular docking and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly malignant central nervous system tumor with an exceptionally poor prognosis. The neuropeptide Galanin is implicated in GBM development, but its specific molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential remain unclear. In this study, we integrate Mendelian randomization (MR) and network toxicology approaches to systematically characterize the pharmacological activity and mechanistic underpinnings of Galanin in GBM.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of galanin in glioblastoma (GBM) by combining Mendelian randomization, network analysis, molecular docking, and experimental validation. The findings suggest a causal link between galanin and GBM and propose potential molecular mechanisms and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Dietary sulforaphane in cancer chemoprevention: epigenetic regulation and PRMT5-MEP50 complex inhibition-a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Cancer chemoprevention using dietary bioactive compounds has emerged as a promising, cost-effective strategy to reduce global cancer incidence and mortality. Sulforaphane (SFN), an isothiocyanate abundant in cruciferous vegetables, has attracted considerable attention for its pleiotropic anticancer effects.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines the chemopreventive mechanisms of dietary sulforaphane (SFN), focusing on its epigenetic regulation and inhibition of the PRMT5-MEP50 complex. The findings suggest that SFN modulates gene expression through epigenetic pathways and disrupts oncogenic signaling, supporting its potential as a cost-effective cancer prevention strategy.

papers.title: Integrated computational and experimental evaluation of natural products targeting PGM/AlgC and HisIE in multidrug-resistant respiratory pathogens.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative respiratory pathogens has reduced the effectiveness of conventional antimicrobial therapies and created a need for antibacterial strategies targeting bacterial metabolic and virulence-associated functions. AlgC, a phosphomannomutase/phosphoglucomutase involved in cell-envelope and exopolysaccharide biosynthesis, and the bifunctional histidine-biosynthesis enzyme HisIE represent potentially relevant bacterial targets.
papers.summary: This study computationally screens natural products against two bacterial enzymes (AlgC and HisIE) that are potential drug targets in multidrug-resistant respiratory pathogens, followed by experimental validation. The findings identify promising natural product hits that may serve as leads for new antibacterial strategies.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of Mannose Metabolism-Related Biomarkers in COPD Through Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Analysis: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) represents a progressive respiratory disorder marked by sustained airflow restriction and ongoing inflammatory processes. Recently, mannose metabolism has emerged as a significant factor in chronic disease development. This investigation explored how mannose metabolism-related genes (MMRGs) contribute to COPD pathogenesis and evaluated their utility as candidate diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This pilot study identifies mannose metabolism-related genes as potential biomarkers for COPD using integrated bioinformatics and machine learning, suggesting a novel role for mannose metabolism in COPD pathogenesis and offering candidate diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: UNKAI: A Protein Functional Identity Prediction Model Based on ESM-C Latent Representations and the Attention Mechanism.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of genome sequencing technologies has led to the accumulation of a vast number of protein sequences in public databases. However, a substantial proportion of these proteins remain functionally uncharacterized. Concurrently, the expansion of protein sequence data has enabled the development of protein language models (pLMs). By distilling billions of years of evolutionary history into a latent representational space, these models have acquired an unprecedented capacity to predict both the tertiary structures and functions of proteins. In this study, we developed a deep lea
papers.summary: UNKAI is a new deep learning model that predicts protein function from sequence by combining ESM-C language model embeddings with an attention mechanism. It addresses the challenge of functionally uncharacterized proteins in public databases, leveraging evolutionary information captured by protein language models to improve functional annotation.

papers.title: Molecular docking and dynamics simulation studies uncover the host-pathogen protein-protein interactions in soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merr.) and Groundnut bud necrosis virus: first report.
papers.abstract: Soybean is a widely consumed oilseed crop with economic importance. It is enriched with numerous bioactive compounds that have health-promoting properties. Groundnut bud necrosis virus (GBNV) affects many agriculturally important crops, such as soybean, resulting in crop losses. GBNV is a single-stranded RNA virus from the genus Orthotospovirus and family Bunyaviridae. It is transmitted by insect vectors (thrips) and is further aggravated by secondary transmission from infected plants to others in the same field. There are no commercially available drugs against GBNV; thus, there is a need to
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and dynamics simulations to investigate host-pathogen protein-protein interactions between soybean and Groundnut bud necrosis virus (GBNV), providing the first reported structural insights into how the virus interacts with host proteins. The findings may inform future strategies for developing resistance or therapeutic interventions against GBNV in soybean.

papers.title: Pan-cancer profiles of mesothelin (MSLN) unveil diagnostic potential and therapeutic targetability of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Mesothelin (MSLN) is a cell surface glycoprotein that is often over-expressed in various malignancies of humans and has been suggested as a potential therapeutic and diagnostic target. However, its expression profile, clinical implications and drug-targeting potential are not fully understood and needs to be investigated across various cancer types.
papers.summary: This study provides a pan-cancer analysis of mesothelin (MSLN) expression, revealing its overexpression across multiple tumor types and highlighting its diagnostic and therapeutic potential, particularly in pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The findings support MSLN as a promising biomarker and drug target for pancreatic cancer.

papers.title: Cavity-Filling Mutations as a Strategy to Stabilize Prefusion Viral Fusion Proteins for Vaccine Design.
papers.abstract: Enveloped viruses use metastable fusion proteins to enter host cells through large-scale conformational rearrangements. The prefusion conformation represents a higher-energy metastable state that irreversibly refolds into a lower-energy postfusion conformation during membrane fusion. Although the prefusion state contains the key neutralizing epitopes, it represents an ideal target for vaccine development. However, because of the instability of the prefusion state, the development of a viable vaccine and the determination of the prefusion state are both major challenges. Building on advances in
papers.summary: This paper explores cavity-filling mutations as a strategy to stabilize the metastable prefusion conformation of viral fusion proteins, which is a key target for vaccine development. By filling internal cavities, these mutations can reduce the energy of the prefusion state, potentially improving protein stability without compromising neutralizing epitopes. The approach offers a promising avenue for designing more effective vaccines against enveloped viruses.

papers.title: Advancing recombinant protein production in CHO cells through metabolic engineering.
papers.abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells serve as the predominant platform for producing recombinant therapeutic proteins in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, the production capacity of which relies heavily on efficient protein synthesis, folding, and secretion pathways. However, during high-density and prolonged cultivation, these cells frequently encounter bottlenecks-including excessive lactate and ammonia accumulation, redox imbalance, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress-which ultimately constrain both the yield and quality of target protein. To overcome these limitations, metabolic engineering
papers.summary: This review discusses metabolic engineering strategies to improve recombinant protein production in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells, focusing on overcoming bottlenecks like lactate/ammonia buildup, redox imbalance, and ER stress. It highlights approaches to enhance protein synthesis, folding, and secretion pathways for better yield and quality in biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

papers.title: Computational design of immunogenic peptide-ligand conjugates for targeted therapy against Nipah virus infection.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) poses a major risk to global public health due to its high infectivity and associated mortality rates. Currently, no licensed vaccines or antiviral medications are available for NiV infection, leaving clinical management limited to supportive care. The viral receptor glycoprotein responsible for binding NiV to host cell receptors (ephrin-B2/B3) represents an ideal therapeutic target. This study proposes a novel peptide-ligand conjugate (PLC) immunotherapeutic approach that exploits pre-existing immune responses in NiV-endemic populations to selectively target and eliminate in
papers.summary: This study computationally designs peptide-ligand conjugates (PLCs) that target the Nipah virus receptor-binding glycoprotein, aiming to exploit pre-existing immune responses in endemic populations for targeted immunotherapy. The approach offers a novel strategy for treating Nipah virus infection, for which no licensed vaccines or antivirals currently exist.
